title: Radical cystectomy with ileal conduit
subtitle: Remove the bladder and nodes, isolate ileum, join the ureters over stents

sources.title: EAU Guidelines on Muscle-invasive and Metastatic Bladder Cancer
BAUS procedure-specific patient information and consent guidance

indications: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (after neoadjuvant chemotherapy where suitable), or high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease failing BCG.
contraindications: Short bowel or inflammatory bowel disease (choose another segment or diversion).
preparation: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis; MDT decision; neoadjuvant chemotherapy considered.
Stoma siting and counselling by the stoma nurse.
Consent: high complication rate, bleeding, leak, bowel obstruction, stoma, sexual function, kidney function.
positioning: Supine with slight Trendelenburg and the table broken, or low lithotomy for women; arms out and padded.
equipment: Major laparotomy set, vascular clamps, staplers, ureteric single-J stents, fine absorbable sutures, stoma appliance, drains.
anatomy: Ureters (blood supply runs alongside), bladder pedicles, iliac vessels and nodes, rectum, the urethra; in women the uterus and anterior vaginal wall; terminal ileum and its mesentery.
criticalSafety: Keep the ureteric blood supply and send ureteric margins if needed.
Spare the last 15 to 20 cm of terminal ileum.
commonErrors: Ureters cut too long and ischaemic, or under tension.
postop: Enhanced recovery; stents out at about 10 to 14 days; stoma training.
Renal function and B12 monitoring long term.

steps.emphasis: Stoma, complications and long-term kidney and bowel effects discussed.
Staging, neoadjuvant chemotherapy and diversion choice confirmed.
The conduit stoma sited in the right iliac fossa by the stoma nurse.
Supine with the table broken and slight Trendelenburg (low lithotomy for women).
Pelvic lymph node dissection: external iliac, obturator and internal iliac, at least to the common iliac bifurcation.
Bleeding from the dorsal venous complex or iliac veins: press, tell, call.
Bladder (with prostate or uterus) intact, ureteric margins labelled.
Restore ileal continuity above the conduit; close the mesenteric window.
Mature the conduit as a spouted stoma at the marked site.
Record both ureteric stents and their removal date.

step.rc.ureters.title: Find and divide the ureters
step.rc.ureters.why: Long, healthy ureters with their blood supply are the basis of a good diversion; a cancerous margin must be found now.
how: Find each ureter at the iliac bifurcation and follow it down to the bladder, keeping its adventitia.
Clip and divide it close to the bladder; send the distal margin for frozen section if indicated.
Bring the left ureter under the sigmoid mesentery to the right side.
pitfalls: Kinking the left ureter under the mesentery.

step.rc.pedicles.title: Bladder pedicles and removal of the specimen
step.rc.pedicles.why: Controlling the lateral and posterior pedicles lets the bladder come out with the prostate (men) or the uterus and anterior vaginal wall (women).
how: Divide the lateral pedicles with staplers, sealing device or ties, keeping away from the rectum.
Develop the plane in front of the rectum, then control the dorsal venous complex and divide the urethra.
pitfalls: Bleeding from the dorsal venous complex.

step.rc.ileal-segment.title: Isolate the ileal segment
step.rc.ileal-segment.why: A 15 to 20 cm segment with good mesentery, taken away from the terminal ileum, makes a conduit that drains well.
how: Measure about 15 to 20 cm of ileum, starting at least 15 to 20 cm from the ileocaecal valve.
Transilluminate the mesentery and divide it keeping the arcades to the segment.
Divide the bowel and place the segment below the restored ileum.

step.rc.uretero-ileal.title: Uretero-ileal anastomoses over stents
step.rc.uretero-ileal.why: Tension-free, well-vascularised joins over stents give the fewest leaks and strictures.
how: Spatulate each ureter and join it to the conduit end-to-side (Bricker) or to each other and the conduit end (Wallace).
Pass a stent up each ureter into the kidney and out through the conduit.
Use fine absorbable sutures, mucosa to mucosa; check no tension or twist.
pitfalls: Too much ureter left and ischaemic.
